record.paper_title: (Two) Open Questions in Stellar Nuclear Physics
record.context_brief: S17(0) extrapolation for the 7Be(p,γ)8B solar-model reaction
record.original_question: How can the zero-energy astrophysical cross-section factor S17(0) for the 7Be(p,γ)8B reaction be extrapolated with 5% or better accuracy when high-precision GSI, Weizmann, and Seattle measurements agree in normalization but have sufficiently different slopes, making the slope-dependent d-wave correction ill determined and capable of reducing S17(0) by as much as 15%?

evidence.quote: reaction cross sections that must be measured with an accuracy of 5% or better are the 7Be(p, γ)8B reaction and the 4He(3He,γ)7Be reaction and the corresponding S17(0) and S34(0) defined in Ref. [8].

However as shown in Fig. 1 the slopes of these three results are sufficiently different. The d-wave correction to S17(0) on the other hand is directly related to this slope, and thus it is ill determined. Since the d-wave correction reduces S17(0) by as much as 15%, it precludes an accurate extrapolation of S17(0).
This issue must be resolved by future high precision measurements of the slope, most likely with 7Be beams [12], so as to allow accurate (5% or better) extrapolation of S17(0).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the proton-capture reaction $^{7}\mathrm{Be}(p,\gamma)^{8}\mathrm{B}$, whose low-energy behavior is encoded in the astrophysical $S$-factor $S_{17}(E)$, defined by
$$S_{17}(E) = E\,\sigma(E)\,\exp\!\bigl(2\pi\eta(E)\bigr),$$
where $\sigma(E)$ is the center-of-mass cross section at relative energy $E$ and $\eta(E)$ is the Sommerfeld parameter for the $p+{}^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ system. The quantity of interest in solar neutrino modeling is the zero-energy value $S_{17}(0)$, obtained by extrapolating measurements taken at center-of-mass energies above roughly $100$ keV down to $E=0$.

Several independent direct-capture measurements of $\sigma(E)$ in the energy range $\sim 100$–$1500$ keV agree on the absolute normalization of $S_{17}(E)$ but differ noticeably in its slope $dS_{17}/dE$. Standard extrapolations decompose $S_{17}$ into an $s$-wave (external direct-capture) piece and a $d$-wave correction whose magnitude at $E=0$ is fixed by matching the slope of the measured $S$-factor; this $d$-wave correction can reduce $S_{17}(0)$ by up to $15\%$.

Problem. Devise a method (theoretical, experimental, or combined) that determines $S_{17}(0)$ to a fractional accuracy of $5\%$ or better, despite the present spread in the measured slopes $dS_{17}/dE$ and the resulting ambiguity in the $d$-wave correction. Equivalently: identify constraints (e.g., from precision slope measurements with a $^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ beam, from sub-threshold pole structure, or from microscopic/ab initio nuclear structure calculations) sufficient to pin down the $d$-wave contribution to $S_{17}(0)$ within this tolerance.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent precision direct measurements (e.g., Junghans et al. with implanted $^7$Be targets) and global R-matrix/ANC analyses report $S_{17}(0)\approx 20.8\text{–}22.3$ eV b with combined experimental+theoretical uncertainties at roughly the 5–8% level. Solar Fusion II/III evaluations and recent ab initio calculations have narrowed but not fully eliminated the d-wave/extrapolation uncertainty. Thus the extrapolation goal of ≤5% accuracy is essentially achieved by the recommended evaluations, though theoretical extrapolation error remains comparable to experimental error and continues to be refined.

status_evidence.title: Precision measurement of the 7Be(p,γ)8B cross section with an implanted 7Be target
status_evidence.snippet: Yielded S17(0) = 22.3±0.7(expt)±0.5(theor) eV b, statistical+systematic precision better than ±5%.
status_evidence.claim: Direct measurements have reached ~5% experimental precision on S17(0).

status_evidence.title: Precise measurement of the 7Be(p,γ)8B S-factor
status_evidence.snippet: S17(0) = 22.1±0.6(expt)±0.6(theor) eV b based on data from 116 to 362 keV with 12 theoretical extrapolations.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical extrapolation uncertainty is comparable to experimental, partially addressing the slope/d-wave issue.

status_evidence.title: s-wave scattering lengths for the 7Be+p system from an R-matrix analysis
status_evidence.snippet: R-matrix analyses constrain low-energy slope and sub-threshold pole behavior, reducing extrapolation error.
status_evidence.claim: Modern R-matrix analyses help control the d-wave/slope ambiguity.

status_evidence.title: Study of radiative proton capture by the 7Be nucleus with ab initio approaches
status_evidence.snippet: Ab initio calculations aim to determine S-factor in measured and unmeasured energy regions.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing ab initio work continues to refine the theoretical extrapolation.
